item.text:
{
  "critic_suggestions": "The three plotted pairs and axis ticks match the raw data: MSE is 9 at b = 0, 2.25 at b = 1.5, and 0 at b = 3. Equal horizontal spacing and the discrete presentation are appropriate. However, the title extends beyond the right edge and is truncated; wrap it across two lines while preserving every word. The explanatory caption is embedded in the image, violating the caption-exclusion requirement, and its first line is also clipped. Remove the caption from the image and retain it separately in the manuscript. All three coordinate labels touch or slightly overlap their markers; bottom-align the labels at their specified elevated anchors to create clear separation. The supplied image has a 4:3 aspect ratio rather than the requested 3:2 canvas; export at 9 × 6 inches and verify that all text and markers fit within the final bounds.",
  "revised_description": "Create fig_intercept_error in R using ggplot2 as a publication-ready discrete scatter plot. Initialize the complete dataset explicitly as data.frame(b = c(0, 1.5, 3), mse = c(9, 2.25, 0)). Map numeric b to horizontal position and numeric mse to vertical position. Plot exactly (0, 9), (1.5, 2.25), and (3, 0). Do not include connecting lines, fitted curves, interpolation, uncertainty intervals, additional observations, underlying observation-level data, or MAE values.

Export on a 9 × 6 inch landscape canvas, equivalent to 2700 × 1800 pixels at 300 dpi. Use white plot and panel backgrounds and DejaVu Sans throughout. Set outer margins to 18 pt top, 24 pt right, 16 pt bottom, and 18 pt left. Check the final export for clipping.

Use geom_point() with shape 21, size 4.2, stroke 0.6, fill #0072B2, outline #004A73, and full opacity. Draw the markers above the grid. Marker appearance must not encode another variable.

Label the horizontal axis 'Added intercept correction b' and the vertical axis 'Mean squared error'. Use continuous horizontal positions with breaks exactly at 0, 1.5, and 3, displayed as those strings. Set vertical breaks to 0, 2.25, 4.5, 6.75, and 9, without unnecessary trailing zeros. Use horizontal viewing limits of −0.35 to 3.35 and vertical viewing limits of −0.6 to 10.2, with no additional scale expansion. The space below zero provides marker clearance and does not represent negative MSE measurements.

Render axis titles at 13 pt, regular weight, in #222222, with 10 pt separation from tick labels. Render tick labels horizontally at 11 pt in #222222. Draw bottom and left axis lines in #6B7280 with 0.4 mm linewidth and outward ticks of 3 pt with 0.35 mm linewidth. Omit top and right panel borders. Show only horizontal major gridlines at the specified vertical ticks, using #E5E7EB and 0.3 mm linewidth; omit vertical and minor gridlines.

Annotate the points with the exact strings '(0, 9)', '(1.5, 2.25)', and '(3, 0)'. Place their anchors at (0, 9.45), (1.5, 2.70), and (3, 0.45), respectively. Use horizontal centering and bottom alignment, equivalent to hjust = 0.5 and vjust = 0 in geom_text(), so the labels extend upward from these anchors and remain clearly separated from the markers. Use 12 pt regular text in #1F2937, converting point sizes to the geometry's native units as needed. Preserve all strings exactly.

Render the title as 'Recorded Mean Squared Error\nat Three Intercept Corrections', using a deliberate line break to preserve the complete wording within the canvas. Use 16 pt bold DejaVu Sans in #111827, align the title with the left edge of the plotting panel, and leave 12 pt below it. Do not display a legend.

Do not render a caption, footnote, or explanatory paragraph anywhere within the image. Keep the following text separately as the manuscript caption: 'Three recorded corrections evaluated on the same five synthetic observations used to determine the correction. No stochastic repetitions or held-out evaluation.'

The finished figure must clearly communicate only the three recorded arithmetic results, with no claim about unmeasured corrections or predictive generalization."
}
